goal: Build the repeatable targeted story-generation pipeline FAB-9 and FAB-10 name: an explicit machine-readable target manifest, a deterministic validator that reuses the merged Reader/content-integrity semantics, and a bounded generate/validate/repair batch runner that writes candidate FILES only.
non_goals: Publishing, staging or inserting any generated story into the database
Rewriting, re-scoring or re-validating the 204 already-published stories
Fixing the forms[0] ingestion defect, reseeding vocabulary, or backfilling source_id
Choosing a production writer model, or running a broad writer bakeoff
Changing Reader segmentation, the content-integrity gate, or the accepted debt baseline
Editing the workflows that invoke this pipeline — their CLI contract is consumed, not changed
acceptance_criteria: A story's generation target is one versioned machine-readable manifest covering band, required words with their selection cohort and reason, the allowed-vocabulary boundary, encounter expectations and format constraints
Target cohorts cover newly-taught vocabulary, under-covered vocabulary, explicit coverage gaps and an explicitly requested word set
A required word counts as present only when the canonical Reader engine resolves it as its own token, never by substring
Validation is deterministic, returns machine-readable diagnostics naming each failure and its offending word or line, and never returns accepted for a failing candidate
Reader resolvability and publishability reuse src/storyReading.js and storyVocabAudit.publishable rather than a second definition of a known word
The repair/retry loop is bounded, classifies each diagnostic as repairable or requiring a fresh draft, and stops at the limit
An interrupted batch resumes without regenerating or duplicating an already-accepted candidate
generate-targeted-stories.mjs writes only files under data/story-candidates/<batch>/ and has no database write capability, asserted by a spec
verification: npx vitest run storyTargetManifest.test.mjs storyCandidateValidation.test.mjs storyBatchState.test.mjs storyPipelineContract.test.mjs
stop_conditions: Any change would be needed to Reader segmentation, the content-integrity gate or the accepted baseline to make generated stories pass
Making a candidate pass would require adding or altering a production vocabulary row
The evidence would only support a writer-model decision, which is a separate workstream
A required word cannot be placed naturally and the only remaining option is keyword stuffing
notes: main already carries .github/workflows/story-pilot.yml and llm-bench.yml, which invoke generate-targeted-stories.mjs and dump-story-corpus.mjs with a fixed CLI and expect candidates under data/story-candidates/<batch>/. Those scripts are absent from main — the earlier FAB-9 code was never merged. This task implements that contract from current main rather than reviving the unmerged branch, so the merged workflows become functional instead of forked. Risk r2: story-matching and content semantics, no scheduler, migration, native or CI authority. production_effect read-only: the corpus dump reads live Supabase with the service key and nothing writes.
